data.description:
Latent robustness gap found by the LLM code review of Gerrit 1905 (C4). scripts/gen_config_reference.py::_lifecycle_index() uses dict.setdefault when mapping a canonical schema key to its lifecycle note, so if a single canonical replacement key is ever the target of MORE THAN ONE cfg deprecation alias and/or tombstone, only the first-encountered note survives and the rest are silently dropped from docs/config-reference.md.

No current collision exists (each cfg replacement key is targeted exactly once in rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY+tombstones()), so today's generated output is correct — this is a defensive fix, not a live bug. Fix: accumulate notes per canonical key (join multiple lifecycle notes) instead of setdefault, and add a held-out test that seeds two deprecations/tombstones pointing at the same replacement and asserts BOTH notes render in that key's row.

AC:\n- [ ] _lifecycle_index accumulates all lifecycle notes for a canonical key (no silent drop).\n- [ ] A test seeds a 2-alias collision and asserts both notes appear in the key's config-reference.md row.\n- [ ] gen --check stays clean; existing oracle still GREEN.
data.title: Harden gen_config_reference _lifecycle_index against multi-alias canonical-key collisions
